_meta.indication: ERAXIS is indicated for treatment of candidemia and other forms of Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis) and esophageal candidiasis

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind study of ERAXIS vs fluconazole in candidemia and other Candida infections (trial name not stated in label)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind; ERAXIS 200 mg loading then 100 mg maintenance once daily IV vs IV fluconazole 800 mg loading then 400 mg maintenance; stratified by APACHE II score and presence/absence of neutropenia
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with candidemia and/or other forms of invasive candidiasis; patients with Candida endocarditis, osteomyelitis or meningitis or C. krusei infection excluded
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary analysis of global response at the end of IV therapy in the modified intent-to-treat (MITT) population; successful global response required clinical cure/improvement plus documented or presumed microbiological eradication
pivotal_trials.n: 256 patients randomized and treated (131 anidulafungin, 125 fluconazole); 245 in MITT population (127 ERAXIS, 118 fluconazole)
pivotal_trials.result: Global success at end of IV therapy: ERAXIS 96/127 (75.6%) vs fluconazole 71/118 (60.2%); treatment difference 15.42% (95% CI 3.9, 27.0)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Phase 3 double-blind, double-dummy, randomized study of ERAXIS vs oral fluconazole in esophageal candidiasis (trial name not stated in label)
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, double-dummy, randomized; ERAXIS 100 mg loading IV Day 1 then 50 mg/day IV vs oral fluconazole 200 mg loading then 100 mg/day; treatment 7 days beyond symptom resolution (min 14, max 21 days)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with esophageal candidiasis; of 442 culture-confirmed patients most (91%) had C. albicans; of 280 tested, 237 (84.6%) were HIV positive
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Endoscopic outcome (endoscopic success = cure or improvement) at end of therapy in the clinically evaluable population
pivotal_trials.n: 601 treated (300 ERAXIS, 301 fluconazole); clinically evaluable population 231 anidulafungin, 236 fluconazole
pivotal_trials.result: Endoscopic success at EOT: ERAXIS 225/231 (97.4%) vs fluconazole 233/236 (98.7%); difference -1.3% (95% CI -3.8%, 1.2%). Higher endoscopic relapse 2 weeks post-treatment: 120/225 (53.3%) anidulafungin vs 45/233 (19.3%) fluconazole

key_safety: Overall ERAXIS safety assessed in 929 individuals. In candidemia, treatment-related AEs reported in >=2.0% of subjects: at least 1 treatment-related AE 24.4% vs fluconazole 26.4%; diarrhea 3.1%, hypokalemia 3.1%. Possible histamine-mediated symptoms (rash, urticaria, flushing, pruritus, dyspnea, hypotension) reported. Hepatic effects: laboratory abnormalities in liver function tests seen in volunteers and patients
target_moa: Anidulafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin that inhibits glucan synthase (present in fungal but not mammalian cells), inhibiting formation of 1,3-β-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall

description.text: Added pediatric patients 1 month of age and older to the indication for treatment of candidemia and other Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis)

citations.quote: Supplement 027	Addition of the pediatric population 1 month of age and older to the approved indication for treatment of candidemia and other forms of Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis); this supplement was submitted to fulfill deferred postmarketing requirement (PMR) #311-1, listed in the February 17, 2006 NDA approval letter.

summary.text: ERAXIS (anidulafungin) NDA 21-632 was originally submitted April 25, 2003, received approvable letters in 2004 and 2005, and was approved on the date of this 2006 letter for esophageal candidiasis, together with NDA 21-948 for candidemia and other Candida infections; a deferred pediatric study was required as a postmarketing commitment under PREA

citations.quote: NDA 21-632, originally submitted on April 25, 2003, received an approvable letter on May 21, 2004.

NDA 21-948 was submitted on August 18, 2005 and received on August 18, 2005. This new drug application provides for the use of Eraxis (anidulafungin) for Injection for the treatment of patients with candidemia and other forms of *Candida* infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis).
We completed our review of these applications, as amended. They are approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the agreed-upon labeling text.
Your deferred pediatric studies required under section 2 of the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) are considered required postmarketing study commitments.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of candidemia and other forms of Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis) in pediatric patients ages zero months to sixteen years; final report submission February 17, 2011
